name: Priya Osei-Nakamura
creator: Priya Osei-Nakamura
description: Considered the preeminent literary voice of Tier 3 life, Osei-Nakamura writes dense, interior novels about the slow erosion of middle-tier identity under corponation pressure. Her breakthrough novel 'The Accountable Hours' (2207) spent nineteen months on the HelixCorp Recommended Reading list before she publicly burned the endorsement in a neural-broadcast event watched by 4.2 million simultaneous feeds. Her prose is architectural — long sentences that fold back on themselves like the corridors of mid-stack housing.
medium: neural feed serialization and physical hardprint editions
cultural_impact: Osei-Nakamura is the writer most frequently cited by Tier 3 readers as 'the one who named what I couldn't.' Her work gave language to the particular shame of being comfortable enough not to revolt and poor enough to feel the walls.
controversy: The endorsement burning caused HelixCorp to quietly withdraw distribution support for her subsequent titles, making physical editions scarce and neural feed access throttled — which only increased her mystique and black-market print circulation.
story_hooks: A HelixCorp cultural affairs operative is assigned to rehabilitate Osei-Nakamura's relationship with the corponation — through persuasion or fabrication.
A Tier 2 reader has built an entire philosophy of life around misreading one of her novels, and she discovers this when they appear at a rare physical signing.
Her next manuscript contains what appears to be a detailed and accurate description of an unreported corponation atrocity — and she claims she simply imagined it.
